description: This table on the San Diego Regional Water Quality Control Board's sewage pollution page lists the spill and transboundary flow events that the US Section of the International Boundary and Water Commission reports under its discharge permit for the South Bay International Wastewater Treatment Plant. Each row gives start and end dates, the event type, the location (such as the Hollister Street Pump Station, Smuggler's Gulch, Goat Canyon or Silva Drain), an approximate discharge volume, the volume recovered and a note on cause, for example a pump station failure, excess sediment from Mexico or a ruptured drain line. Entries begin on 1 July 2024, and the Tijuana River line counts cumulative wet and dry weather flows from Mexico at 66.1 billion gallons since 11 October 2023, as reported on 30 April 2026. The page updates about weekly and points to the USIBWC water data portal for flow gauge data. Coverage: one border watershed; a web table, not a download. Access: free, with the licence not stated. Caveats: volumes are approximate self-reports, and river flow is not required to be reported to the Water Board. It supports transboundary wastewater failure, pump station reliability and coastal pollution studies, and relates to the Berlin combined sewer overflow monitoring data and the Boston overflow control plan in the catalogue.
